findings.title: Auth generated baseline and snapshot contain stale random role seeds that differ from the committed deterministic model
findings.trigger: Scaffolded Auth baseline was generated from a model containing Role.Create runtime values while the current committed configuration uses explicit stable seeds. Compare generated source/snapshot seed rows with current RoleConfiguration.
findings.impact: Fresh baseline rows differ from the current model contract. A future model-diff scaffold can delete the snapshot role IDs and insert the stable IDs; RoleId FK cascade can then remove UserRoles assignments. The migration and snapshot must be corrected before publication or baseline adoption. No actual data loss or executed migration is claimed.
findings.remediation: Root should regenerate the unpublished Auth baseline/Designer/snapshot from the verified current assembly, retain reviewed paths/tool provenance, then compare target model with current design-time model and execute fresh/adoption tests. Do not silently rewrite existing unmanaged role IDs or run the initial InsertData during adoption.
findings.correction: Initial random seeds rejected; final Auth Up/Designer/snapshot now use the exact committed stable IDs and fixed UTC timestamp. Initial finding and hashes preserved in initial_review. No generated source defect remains identified by this read-only comparison.

Auth: 11 tables/11 PKs/6 FKs and35 indexes reflect the mapped shape. Final regenerated Up/Designer/snapshot role seeds now match the committed stable IDs and timestamp.
Owned Email maps to Users.Email with unique index; UserRoles has unique(UserId,RoleId), RoleId/UserId cascade FKs. LoginHistory/RefreshTokens cascade from Users; friendships restrict user deletes.
PasswordHistory/UserRecoveryCodes lack user FKs in this baseline consistently with their current configuration; do not add relationships as a migration-review side effect.
Refresh token partial unique filter remains RevokedAt IS NULL; expiry semantics remain existing BE-004 and are not fixed by a baseline.
Outbox partial active index, retry default0 and varchar lengths match config. Auth inbox string Status and unique MessageId match its explicit mapping.
Friendship xmin is Npgsql row-version metadata; generated SQL/provider execution must verify system-column handling.
TwoFactorSecret remains varchar1024; the design-time baseline contains no key material or encrypted user values. Runtime DataProtection key management is outside this review.
Category: Categories +OutboxMessages table shape, self-parent nullable FK, varchar lengths/defaults, xmin metadata and8 indexes match CategoryDbContext/CategoryConfiguration/OutboxMessageConfiguration.
No seed rows or destructive Up operations. Query filters are runtime model behavior, not automatically physical database constraints.
Messaging: Messages +InboxMessages +OutboxMessages match inline MessagingDbContext and its outbox configuration.
MessageId in convention-mapped Messaging inbox is text and Status integer; it intentionally differs from Auth explicit inbox string mapping. No new inbox index is silently added.
Message.Id ValueGeneratedNever, JSON attachment string storage, five message indexes and three outbox indexes match current code; no cross-service user FKs are introduced.
Collaboration: Both migration IDs match CollaborationDatabaseStartup constants and the reviewed adoption ceiling.
Baseline creates collaboration schema and comments/InboxMessages/OutboxMessages, with three PKs and six indexes. The mapped xmin remains a provider system column.
Reply upgrade adds the six properties and one composite index. The final target model and snapshot differ from the baseline target only by these insertions.
The new Down drops the composite index and six columns, destroying reply data. The earlier Down drops the three service tables.
No seed or raw SQL operation in either Up. Fresh and reviewed-prefix adoption remain executable gates.

sql_and_adoption_risks: All three Up methods are initial schema creation; running them against existing unmanaged tables is not an upgrade/adoption strategy.
Down drops all service tables and data (Auth11,Category2,Messaging3); never use against working data as an automatic rollback.
Guarded adoption must prove full schema equivalence before inserting migration history and must skip initial data/DDL execution. Existing Auth Role.Id and UserRoles references must remain unchanged.
Future role data changes for adopted arbitrary IDs require an explicit name-aware migration; model-managed seed PK replacement is not safe for those databases.
Indexes/constraints create locks and can fail on incompatible existing data. No lock-duration benchmark, SQL script review or physical index/FK verification was executed by this reviewer.
No raw migrationBuilder.Sql, Up AlterColumn/DropTable/DeleteData/UpdateData operations were found; absence of these calls does not certify provider-generated SQL.
Auth pending-model warning suppression makes an explicit model/snapshot comparison gate important; no model-differ was run by this read-only reviewer.

execution.method: Full source reads, static operation counts, SHA256 and full Designer/snapshot model-body equality; no source changes.

limits: These migration sources are currently ignored and not staged; this review gives no permission for force-add.
Per-file continuation coverage outside these generated9 files is not promoted by supplemental configuration reads.
Root must integrate verified regenerated hashes and exact provider/model-differ evidence before claiming T08 acceptance.

This update corrects only generated-source review. The separate adversarial schema-guard review remains NEEDS WORK until root records its own GREEN evidence; it is not resolved by source regeneration.
